marketing.headline: Learn it loud enough to remember.
marketing.lede: Turn any pair of things — a word and its translation, a term and its definition — into a deck you can flip, quiz, write, match, and listen through until it sticks.
marketing.heroNote: Free to start · no card required
marketing.modesTitle: One deck. Five ways to be tested.
marketing.modesSub: Flip to check yourself. Quiz to recognize. Write to produce. Match to move fast. Listen when your eyes are busy.
marketing.librarySub: Organize decks into sets by class, language, or exam — color-coded so your Chinese lessons never blur into your bar prep.
marketing.statBody: Reviewing a card right before you'd forget it beats reviewing it twice as often on a fixed schedule. Zipdeck times every review around that exact moment, so the minutes you do spend studying go further.
marketing.builtFor: Built for people learning something, anything.

flip.title: See it, say it
flip.body: A prompt on the front, the answer on the back. Rate your own recall honestly and the deck adjusts what you see next.

quiz.title: Pick the right one
quiz.body: Multiple choice built from your own deck, so the wrong answers are things you'd genuinely mix up — not random noise.

write.title: Type it from scratch
write.body: No multiple choice to lean on. The slowest mode, and the one most likely to make a word stay for good.

match.title: Pair them off
match.body: Prompts on one side, answers on the other. Clear the board by matching pairs — misses come back sooner.
match.hint: tap a prompt, then its pair

audio.title: Hear it first
audio.body: The prompt plays out loud. Reveal when you've got it, then rate the recall. Built for commutes and walks.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how Zipdeck collects, uses, and stores information when you use https://zipdeck.app and the Zipdeck apps. It is written for people signing in with Google as well as with email and password.
privacy.whoBody: Zipdeck is a flashcard study service at https://zipdeck.app. It helps you create decks, study them (flip, quiz, write, match, and audio), and keep review schedules. This policy applies to that service.
privacy.googleBody: If you choose Continue with Google, Zipdeck uses Google Identity Services with only the basic sign-in scopes (openid, email, and profile). Google then shares with us:
privacy.googleItemName: Your Google account name, used as your Zipdeck display name.
privacy.googleItemEmail: Your Google account email, used as your Zipdeck login email.
privacy.googleItemId: A stable Google user id (the “sub” claim), stored so we can recognize the same Google account on later visits.
privacy.googleUse: We use that Google user data only to create a Zipdeck account, sign you in, and keep your email up to date if it changes at Google. We do not request access to Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Contacts, or any other Google product.
privacy.googleNot: We do not sell Google user data. We do not use it for advertising. We do not share it with other companies for their marketing. We do not use it for any purpose other than operating your Zipdeck account.
privacy.accountBody: If you register with email and password, we store your name, email, and a hashed password (not the password itself). Every account also stores study preferences such as language, theme, and how cards are scheduled. Signed-in sessions use a token we keep in your browser’s local storage so you stay logged in on that device.
privacy.studyBody: Content you add — decks, cards, sets, ratings, and review dates — is stored so the app can show it back to you and schedule reviews. Shared library catalogs are the same for everyone; copies you add to My Decks belong to your account.
privacy.aiBody: If you use Create With AI, the prompt you type and the generated cards are sent to Google’s Gemini API so a deck can be created. Do not include information in a prompt that you would not want processed by that service.
privacy.hostingBody: Zipdeck runs on Amazon Web Services (Lightsail). Account and deck data are stored in our database on that host. Backups of that database may be kept so we can restore the service if something fails.
privacy.shareBody: We share data with the processors needed to run Zipdeck: Amazon Web Services for hosting, and Google for optional Google sign-in and optional AI deck generation. We may also disclose information if required by law. We do not sell your personal information.
privacy.rightsBody: You can edit your profile and study settings in the app. You can stop using Google sign-in by not connecting that method on a new account. To access, correct, or delete your account and the decks stored with it, contact us using the details below and write from the email on the account. We will delete the account and its study data when we can identify it.
privacy.childrenBody: Zipdeck is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them.
privacy.changesBody: We may update this policy. The “Last updated” date at the top will change when we do. The current version will always be at https://zipdeck.app/privacy.
privacy.contactBody: For privacy questions or deletion requests, email  support@zipdeck.app. Write from the email on the Zipdeck account so we can find it.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How Zipdeck works, from your first deck to spaced review.
help.startIntro: Zipdeck is a place to make flashcards and study them when they are due. You sign in once; the same account works on the website and the mobile apps.
help.startStep1: Open My Decks and create a deck, or copy one from Sample Sets.
help.startStep2: Add cards with a front (the prompt) and a back (the answer). A hint and a picture are optional.
help.startStep3: Tap Study, pick a mode, and rate each card. Zipdeck schedules the next time you should see it.
help.startHint: Nothing due yet is normal on a new deck. Study anyway — the first pass puts cards on the calendar.
help.decksIntro: A deck is one pile of cards on a topic. A set is a folder of decks, such as a class or a textbook.
help.decksCardsBody: Each card has a front and a back. You can add an optional hint. Front and back can use different languages, which helps with vocabulary.
help.decksImagesBody: Pro can put a photo on the front or the back — useful for anatomy, maps, or words you remember as a picture. JPG, PNG, or GIF up to 5 MB.
help.decksSetsBody: Open Manage Sets to group decks. You can still study one deck on its own.
help.decksCsvBody: Import or export a deck as CSV if you already have a spreadsheet of prompts and answers.
help.decksCsvHow: Open a deck, then tap Import CSV. Export CSV downloads the same three-column layout, so you can edit in a spreadsheet and import it back.
help.decksCsvColumns: Use a comma-separated UTF-8 .csv file. Column 1 is the front (prompt), column 2 is the back (answer). A third column is an optional hint.
help.decksCsvHeader: A header row is optional. If you include one, the first two columns must be named front and back, or question and answer. A hint header in the third column is fine.
help.decksCsvQuote: Wrap any cell that contains a comma or a quotation mark in double quotes. Write a quote inside a cell as two quotes together ("").
help.decksCsvRules: Every card needs both a front and a back. Blank rows are skipped. Tab-separated files, semicolon-separated files, and Excel workbooks (.xlsx) are not accepted.
help.decksCsvSheet: From Excel or Google Sheets, use File → Download or Save as → CSV UTF-8, and keep commas as the separator.
help.decksOrderBody: Drag the handle or use the arrows to put cards in the order you want. Deck order is one of the study-order options in Settings.
help.studyIntro: Study from a deck (or a mix). You choose how you want to practice. After Flip and Audio you rate the card; Quiz, Write, and Match score from what you picked or typed.
help.ratingsIntro: After the answer is shown, compare what you thought of with what is on the card, then tap one of these buttons.
help.ratingsMissed: Tap this when your answer is wrong or you could not recall it. If you are only partly right, be strict: if it would count as a fail in real life, it counts as Missed here too. You will typically use this about 5–20% of the time.
help.ratingsHard: Tap this when your answer is correct, but you had doubts or it took a long time to recall.
help.ratingsGotIt: Tap this when your answer is correct, but it took some mental effort to recall. When you use Zipdeck as intended, this should be the button you tap most often — typically about 80–95% of the time.
help.ratingsEasy: Tap this when your answer is correct and it took no mental effort to recall.
help.studyRatings: Missed brings the card back soon. Hard keeps it close. Got it and Easy stretch the wait. Those ratings feed SM-2, below.
help.studyAfter: When a session ends you can continue the rest of the deck, restart what you just studied, or drill only Missed or Hard cards. Ratings stay; only the queue changes.
help.sm2Intro: Zipdeck uses SuperMemo 2 (SM-2), a spaced-repetition schedule. It shows a card again just as you are about to forget it — not every day, and not so late that it is gone.
help.sm2How: Each time you rate a card, SM-2 updates two things: how soon it is due, and how “easy” that card is for you. Cards you miss reset to a short wait. Cards you keep getting right wait longer each time: tomorrow, then about a week, then weeks.
help.sm2Ratings: That is why Missed and Hard are useful, not a failure. They tell the scheduler the memory is still fragile. Got it and Easy tell it the memory is sticking, so Zipdeck spends your time on weaker cards instead.
help.sm2Why: Cramming dumps everything into short-term memory. Spacing reviews over days is what moves a fact into long-term recall. SM-2 is the calendar for that.
help.demoSm2Start: New card — rate Got it to schedule it.
help.libraryIntro: Sample Sets are ready-made decks you can copy into My Decks. Copy what you need, then edit or study like any other deck. Your ratings stay on your copy.
help.aiBenefit: Typing every card by hand is the slow part. Create With AI drafts a deck from a short prompt or a PDF of notes, so you spend time editing and studying instead of formatting. You still own the cards — change anything that is off before you review.
help.aiStep1: Open Create With AI (Pro). Describe the topic, or attach a PDF of lecture notes.
help.aiStep2: Zipdeck builds one deck and fills it with cards. One run uses 1 credit.
help.aiStep3: Open the deck, fix wording, add pictures if you want, then study.
help.aiCredits: Pro includes a monthly credit allowance. Unused included credits reset next month. Extra packs you buy stay until you use them.
help.mixBenefit: New material is easy to over-practice. Old decks sit untouched. A Study Mix pulls several decks (and whole sets) into one session so older cards stay in rotation with what you just learned. Mixed review is what keeps memories from fading between chapters.
help.mixStep1: Open Study Mix (Pro) and create a mix.
help.mixStep2: Tick the decks or sets you want in one pile.
help.mixStep3: Study the mix like a deck. Due cards from every source show up together.
help.demoMixAfter: One mix. Old and new cards share the queue.
help.proIntro: Studying, decks, sets, and Sample Sets are included. Pro adds Create With AI, Study Mix, card pictures, and the same login on every device.
help.proItemAi: Create With AI — draft a deck from a prompt or PDF.
help.proItemMix: Study Mix — combine decks so older material stays in rotation.
help.proItemImages: Pictures on the front or back of a card.
help.proItemSync: One subscription on the website and both mobile apps.
help.settingsIntro: Language and appearance follow you on every screen. You can also sort My Decks by name or last studied. Study options set card order (deck order, reverse, or random) and whether a rated card can return the same day or waits for the SM-2 date. Teacher Mode is on the Classes page if you need to run a class.
help.classesIntro: Anyone can join a class with a 6-character code. Teachers turn on Teacher Mode, create a class, and assign decks. Students get a copy in My Decks, so their ratings are their own.
help.contactBody: Questions, billing issues, or something this page does not cover — email us and we will get back to you.
